To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HIV positive IDUs are more likely to be older, married, have a lower education level and have been using drugs for a longer period of time.

HIV positive IDUs in Myanmar are more likely to be older, married, with lower education, living in the capital city, having higher expenditure on drug use, using drugs to escape from problems, having started injecting at an earlier age, using syringe first time for injecting, sharing syringe at first injection, and having failed drug detoxification programmes.

HIV positive IDUs are significantly associated with the age of first use of drugs, age of first used injection, drug use expenditure and reason for using drugs, education level of the respondent, type of syringe used at first injection, sharing syringe at first injection, failure of drug detox program and returning used syringe in centre.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the risk behaviours among injecting drug users in relation to the spread of HIV/AIDS in Myanmar.
the factors which influence HIV positive IDUs to share their syringes and needles.
the factors that contribute to the spread of HIV infection among IDUs in Myanmar, and the implications of our results for public health policy and practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the risk factors for HIV among IDUs are multifactorial and complex in nature.

the risk factors of HIV among IDUs in Myanmar are multiple and varied, and that the risk factors vary from one region to another, and that the most effective strategy for reducing risk factors is to provide access to sterile injecting equipment, and to educate IDUs about safer sex practices.
the risk factors for HIV transmission among IDUs are the same as in other countries, but the prevalence is much higher in Myanmar.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is an urgent need for the government and other stakeholders to develop a national plan to prevent and control HIV/AIDS among IDUs.
HIV infection is associated with several risk behaviours among IDUs in Myanmar.
HIV positive IDUs in Myanmar are found to be associated with high risk behaviors and the findings of this study will be useful for policy makers and health professionals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HIV epidemic among IDUs is a complex phenomenon and requires a multi-faceted approach for prevention.
the IDUs are willing to change their risky behaviours and are ready to accept health education and intervention programmes.
the IDU population in Myanmar is highly vulnerable to the risk of HIV infection and there is a need to address the issue with a multi-sectorial approach.
